title: Impact of Compulsory Schooling on Wages

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We will use an instrumental variable (IV) approach to estimate the causal impact of compulsory schooling on wages. The compulsory schooling year (z) serves as an instrument for education (x). The key assumption for this approach is that the instrument (z) is correlated with education (x) but only affects wages (y) through its effect on education (x), i.e., the exclusion restriction.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(lmtest)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s68_data.csv")

# First stage regression: education (x) on compulsory schooling year (z) and controls
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)

# Second stage regression: log wages (y) on predicted education (x) from first stage and controls
second_stage <- lm(y ~ predict(first_stage, newdata = data) + controls, data = data)

# Print the coefficient of predicted education (x) from the second stage regression
summary(second_stage)$coefficients[2, 1]

# Robustness check: test for overidentifying restrictions (Sargan test)
ivreg(y ~ x | z + controls, data = data)
sargan_test <- bptest(second_stage, ~z + controls, data = data)
sargan_test$statistic
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect a positive coefficient for education (x) in the second stage regression, indicating that additional compulsory schooling has a positive impact on log wages (y) later in life. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the strength of the relationship between education and wages in the data. The sign and magnitude of the coefficient will provide insights into the causal impact of compulsory schooling on wages.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use compulsory schooling year as an instrument for education.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis suggests that additional compulsory schooling has a negative impact on log wages.
